name: a-later-pipeline-segment-cannot-mutate-what-an-earlier-one-named
description: The second review finding (2026-08-22, 85%, confirmed): the closed mode judged each segment only against its OWN text, so a pipeline whose FIRST segment named the directory through an allowlisted read - here a plain 'find' - set no taint, and the mutating segment behind the pipe named nothing left to match. 'find ~/.claude/keel -type f | xargs rm -f' therefore deleted every file in keel's user-global directory with no deny, no bypass line and no audit row. A segment that NAMES the directory now taints the rest of the command exactly as a 'cd' into it does, so the 'xargs rm' behind the pipe is refused.
